issues.description: Method name mismatch: The problem statement and the template declare and refer to a public method named singFarmSong() in class Farm, but the solution implementation defines a method named playFarmSong() instead. Specifically, problem_statement.md (line 112) instructs to implement singFarmSong(); template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares public void singFarmSong() (line 9). The solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines public void playFarmSong() (line 59). This inconsistency can confuse students and cause tests or example code that call singFarmSong() to fail to compile or run against the solution reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Preferably rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (updating any internal calls to match), so the solution, template, UML, and problem statement all reference the same method name. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to reference playFarmSong(), but renaming the solution is the least disruptive for students following the instructions.

issues.description: The exercise requires a public Farm method named singFarmSong(): the problem statement refers to singFarmSong() and the template provides a public stub method singFarmSong(). However, the solution's public API uses playFarmSong() (public void playFarmSong()) for the same behavior. This naming mismatch (singFarmSong vs playFarmSong) refers to the same conceptual operation (play/sing the farm song) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students mapping the task description and template to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the public API names: rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method in the solution that delegates to playFarmSong(). This ensures the method name in the solution matches the problem statement and template.
